analyst.summary: Torrent Power's headline profit numbers look weak this year (FY26 PAT down ~19%, Q4 down ~70%), but a large part of that is a high FY25 comparison base (a one-time tax-reversal gain) and a regulatory cost item under dispute that the company expects to recover -- not a breakdown in the underlying distribution-and-generation business, which remains a stable, largely-regulated franchise (Ahmedabad/Surat licensed distribution plus Agra/Bhiwandi franchises) with a healthy balance sheet. The company is also mid-way through a large, funded capacity build (renewables toward 10GW by 2030, plus a new thermal plant and the Nabha Power acquisition) that should support growth over the next few years even though it doesn't show up in this year's numbers yet. We keep it on Hold: the business quality and balance sheet support staying invested, but the current valuation already prices in a fair amount of that future growth, leaving limited margin for delays in the capacity build-out.
